title: pixelSplat: 3D Gaussian Splats from Image Pairs for Scalable Generalizable 3D Reconstruction
layout_note: Three columns: on the left a camera frustum with a feature map plane and three pixel rays; in the middle two stacked grey-tinted panels (top: three per-pixel depth histograms; bottom: three depth axes with a Gaussian placed on each), joined by a 'sample' arrow; on the right the same frustum with three coloured Gaussians on the rays. A small MLP glyph under the left frustum feeds both middle panels.
grouping: Two light-grey filled rectangles with dark outlines group the per-pixel distributions and the per-pixel Gaussian parameters. Three pixels are tracked by colour (red, blue, green) through every element: the feature-map cells, the rays, the parameter vectors, the histogram bars, the Gaussian blobs, and the coloured subscripts a, b, c in every formula.
shapes_depth: Cameras are thick black wireframe pyramids opening into thin-line frusta; the feature map is a grey gridded slab with three coloured cells; rays are long straight coloured arrows. Distributions are flat bar histograms on bare axes, one per row. Gaussians are soft blurred coloured ellipses sitting on depth axes and, at the end, on the rays in the frustum. Parameter vectors are small striped coloured bars. The MLP is three tall unfilled rectangles. Arrows are thin black orthogonal connectors. Equations sit inline at each row's ends.
proposed_highlight: No legend or bold name; the probabilistic step is the large grey panel of three histograms at the top centre, and the colour coding of the three pixels makes it read as one prediction per ray.
lesson: Follow three pixels by colour from feature-map cell to ray, depth histogram, sampled Gaussian on a depth axis and finally a blurred Gaussian on its ray inside the camera frustum, so per-pixel prediction reads as geometry.
notes: venue CVPR from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2312.12337). Vector line art with blurred Gaussian blobs.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: generalizable 3D Gaussian prediction from image pairs
taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = per-pixel probabilistic depth prediction (discrete depth distribution sampled with reparameterization)

core.what: three pixels a, b, c each keep one colour (red, blue, green) through every step: feature-map cell and ray, depth-probability histogram, sampled Gaussian position along the ray, and finally a 3-D Gaussian in the right frustum

relations.form: three colour-coded rows inside each of the two middle grey boxes, one per pixel, stacked in the same a, b, c order
left: a camera frustum with the gridded feature map F, three highlighted cells and three coloured rays; right: the same frustum with blurred coloured 3-D Gaussians placed along those rays

F[a], F[b], F[c] go by a curved arrow into network f, which outputs phi (to the top box) and (Sigma, S) (to the bottom box); the top box's 'sample z ~ p_phi(z)' arrow passes to the bottom box, whose tuples feed the right frustum
two stacked grey boxes: the top draws per-pixel depth distributions p_phi(z) as histograms, the bottom draws each ray as a line with the sampled mean mu = h(z) as a blob and opacity alpha = p_phi(z)

channels.colour: colour = pixel identity (red a, blue b, green c), used on cells, rays, parameter vectors, histogram bars, blobs and subscripts; no other colour
channels.shape: frustums = camera space, histograms = probability distributions, blurred ellipses = Gaussians, bars = network f, small striped bars = parameter vectors phi
channels.line: black arrows for flow; coloured arrows for pixel rays
channels.frame: grey-filled boxes = the two probabilistic depth steps

quality.strengths: One channel carries one meaning throughout: a pixel's colour follows it from feature cell through histogram and sampled blob to the final Gaussian, so the per-pixel pipeline reads without labels; the distributions and samples are drawn as data (histograms, blobs on rays) rather than boxes; the 3-D frustums on both ends show the method on its structure.
quality.weaknesses: Formulas are typeset inside the grey boxes (mu = h(z), alpha = p_phi(z)) and as tuples beside them; the curved arrow from F to f and the line from f fanning to six arrows make an indirect, elbowed route; network f is a tiny glyph at bottom left.

insights.structure: Three columns: a left camera frustum with feature map F and three colored rays, a middle pair of grey boxes stacked vertically (top: three depth-probability histograms; bottom: three ray lines with sampled Gaussian means), and a right frustum with the resulting 3-D Gaussians.
insights.data: Each of three pixels a, b, c keeps one color (red, blue, green) everywhere: highlighted cells on F, ray arrows, histogram bars, blurred Gaussian blobs on lines, and the parameter tuples.
insights.emphasis: The consistent per-pixel color triple is the main device; the stochastic step is spelled out by the 'sample z ~ p_phi(z)' arrow running from the top box to the bottom box.
insights.flow: F[a],F[b],F[c] curve down into network f, which fans out right into both boxes; top box feeds the bottom via the sample arrow; bottom box exits right and up through the parameter tuples into the 3-D Gaussian frustum.
insights.avoid: The network f is three bare unlabeled bars and the fan-out lines from f to six arrows are long and thin, making the split into (phi) and (Sigma, S) easy to miss.

arrangement.units: two grey-filled boxes stacked in the middle (probability histograms, Gaussian placement along rays) between unframed 3-D frustums at left and right
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3-D camera frustum with a gridded feature map and three colored pixel rays
arrangement.shared: per-pixel color coding (red/blue/green) runs across all columns
